result.dispatchDesign:
New `executeSkepticRun` in src/cli.ts, mirroring executeReviewRun (cli.ts:2626-2941) with the RE-1 divergences. Signature identical: {workspace, store, sliceId, actor, driver, model?} -> Promise<SkepticRunResult>. Add a `SkepticRunResult` type next to ReviewRunResult (cli.ts:112-122): { sliceId; runId; exitCode; promptPath; eventsPath; resultPath; skepticEvents: ReturnType<typeof ingestWorkerJsonl>; skepticResult?: SkepticResult; challengedReviewEvidenceId?: string; stderr? }.

Steps (reuse review template exactly except where noted):
1. Lookup+guards: slice via store.listSlices().find (cli.ts:2634); validateSliceDispatchContract(slice); target via store.targetById; driver validated against "fixture"+workerDriverIds() with message "Invalid skeptic driver:". Then run the INDEPENDENCE GUARD (see independenceGuard field) right after driver validation, before any artifact/run creation.
2. Read findings to challenge — the SAME pattern readLatestReviewGate uses (cli.ts:4316-4321): const reviewEvidence = store.listEvidence(slice.id).filter(i => i.kind === "review_result" && i.payload.reviewResult).at(-1). If !reviewEvidence -> throw new Error(`No review_result evidence to challenge for slice: ${slice.id}. Run \`swarm review\` first.`). const parsedToChallenge = reviewResultSchema.safeParse(reviewEvidence.payload.reviewResult); if !success -> throw (cannot challenge an unparseable review). Capture challengedReviewEvidenceId = reviewEvidence.id and the parsed ReviewResult.
3. Artifact paths: artifactPath = artifactsDir/slice.id; runId = makeId("agentRun"); resultPath=skeptic-result-${runId}.json, jsonlPath=skeptic-events-${runId}.jsonl, stderrPath=skeptic-stderr-${runId}.log, promptPath=skeptic-prompt-${runId}.md. schemaPath = workspace/schemas/skeptic-result.schema.json; call new writeSkepticResultSchema(schemaPath) (see cliCommand field).
4. Skills: prepareSkillBindings({workspace, targetPath: target.path, artifactPath, runId, role: "skeptic", protocol}).
5. Prompt: new buildSkepticPrompt (see skillBinding/below) listing each frAcFinding + each qualityGate.dimension + each requiredFix + each escalation from the challenged ReviewResult, with DEFAULT-REJECT framing; write to promptPath.
6. AgentRun + heartbeat + started event: attempt = listAgentRuns().filter(r => r.sliceId===slice.id && r.actor===input.actor).length + 1; insertAgentRun({...role:"skeptic", entityType:"slice", entityId:slice.id, actor, driver, status:"running", attempt, eventsPath:jsonlPath,...}); upsertHeartbeat({id:`heartbeat:${actor}`, actor, state:"verifying", detail:"Independent skeptic process started", entityType:"slice", entityId:slice.id}); addEvent(createEvent({type:"skeptic.started", actor, entityType:"slice", entityId:slice.id, payload:{... runId, attempt, promptPath, eventsPath, challengedReviewEvidenceId, challengedReviewStatus: parsed.status, skills:summarizeSkillBinding(...), ...}})).
7. Driver execution branch: fixture branch calls new runFixtureSkeptic({slice, challengedReview}) returning a deterministic SkepticResult, writes resultPath, sets synthetic stdout JSONL ({type:"fixture.skeptic.completed",...}), skepticFinalization={ok:true,structuredResultWritten:true}. Non-fixture branch: adapter=getWorkerDriver(driver)!; WorkerRunSpec{prompt, targetPath, schemaPath, resultPath, model, readOnly:false, resultSchema: skepticResultSchema, driverConfig: protocol.protocol.workers.drivers[driver] ?? {}}; adapter.buildInvocation(spec); spawnWorkerStreaming({..., eventPrefix:"skeptic", resultArtifact:{path, isReady:()=>validateResultArtifact(spec).ok}}); skepticFinalization = adapter.finalize(...).
8. Ingest: if fixture, write jsonl=stdout; skepticEvents = result.workerEvents ?? ingestWorkerJsonl({store, actor, sliceId, driver, jsonl, eventPrefix:"skeptic"}). recordSkillIsolationWarning({...eventPrefix:"skeptic"}).
9. Parse + record run: parsedSkeptic = readSkepticResultFile(resultPath) (new, mirrors readReviewResultFile but uses skepticResultSchema). updateAgentRun(runId, {status: skepticFinalization.ok && parsedSkeptic.ok ? "completed":"failed", sessionId:skepticEvents.sessionId, eventsPath, resultPath if exists, stderrPath if stderr}).
10. THE KEY DIVERGENCE — additive only: if parsedSkeptic.ok, INSERT kind:"finding_challenge" evidence (role context skeptic) with payload {path:resultPath, skepticResult:parsedSkeptic.result, challengedReviewEvidenceId, skepticEvents}; summary `Skeptic ${result.status}: ${result.summary}`. DO NOT call applyReviewOutcome and DO NOT call updateSliceStatus / updateDependenciesFor / insertReviewEscalation / clearResolvedReviewEscalations. Emit skeptic.completed (mirror review.completed payload) and ONE skeptic.finding_challenged event per verdict in findingVerdicts (payload {ref?, dimension?, source, verdict, severity, reasoning, challengedReviewEvidenceId}). Set heartbeat to state "idle" detail "Independent skeptic completed" (NOT blocked — skeptic never gates).
11. Parse-failure branch: mirror ONLY the event/heartbeat side. Set heartbeat state "blocked" detail reason and emit skeptic.failed; DO NOT updateSliceStatus("blocked"), DO NOT insertReviewEscalation (those mutate gate state). This is the explicit divergence from review.failed at cli.ts:2870-2911.
12. refreshCheckpoint calls mirrored with role:"skeptic" (slice) and role:"recovery" (agent_run) — safe, they don't touch the review gate.
13. Return SkepticRunResult.

result.testPlan:
Build first (npx tsc / npm run build) — tests run the BUILT dist/cli.js. Two test files:

A) New tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js — clone the setupWorkspace()/runSwarm() helpers from review-runner.e2e.test.js (init -> target init -> sources add-file -> slices pull against fixtures/templates/invoice-api, refs AC-INV-001.1..3). Each test runs worker (run --driver fixture --actor <worker>), then review (review --driver fixture --actor <reviewer>) to produce a review_result to challenge, then skeptic (skeptic --driver fixture --actor independent-skeptic), then asserts via `observe --events N` JSON.
  (a) DISTINCT role+actor: snapshot.agentRuns has a run with role==="skeptic", actor==="independent-skeptic", driver==="fixture", status==="completed"; assert that skeptic actor !== the worker actor and !== the reviewer actor used.
  (b) records evidence + events: the slice's evidence has an item with kind==="finding_challenge"; recentEvents include type "skeptic.started" and "skeptic.completed"; at least one "skeptic.finding_challenged" event exists (one per verdict).
  (c) independence guard: run `skeptic <slice> --driver fixture --actor <workerActor>` and separately `--actor <reviewerActor>`; wrap runSwarm in try/catch (execFileSync throws on non-zero exit) and assert it threw AND the combined stdout+stderr (err.stdout/err.stderr) matches /must be independent/ (or /distinct/). Also assert NO finding_challenge evidence and NO skeptic agentRun was created for that rejected actor (ledger untouched on guard rejection).
  (d) accept-gate UNCHANGED regression: capture from `observe` BEFORE the skeptic: the slice.status, slice.reviewResult (full object), and the slice-scoped review escalations / activeEscalations. Run the skeptic. Re-observe and assert slice.status, slice.reviewResult, and review-related escalations are deep-equal (byte-identical) — the skeptic mutated none of the gate state. THEN run `verify <slice> --actor deterministic-verifier` and assert it gates on the review_result exactly as review-runner.e2e.test.js does (e.g. accepted review -> Verification passed and the latest command evidence payload.reviewGate.reason === "latest review accepted"), proving readLatestReviewGate still reads ONLY review_result, ignoring finding_challenge. Add a second variant where the underlying review is "blocked" (re-run review --driver fixture is always 'accepted' for fixture with no source mutation, so to exercise the blocked path either use codex fake like review-runner or assert the accepted path; the accepted+verify-passes regression is sufficient to prove additivity for RE-1).

B) tests/schema-parity.test.js — add a fourth roles[] entry: { name:"skeptic", zodSchema:skepticResultSchema, valid:<a valid SkepticResult fixture: status:"upheld", summary, challengedReviewStatus:"accepted", findingVerdicts:[{ref:"AC-1", source:"fr_ac_finding", verdict:"real", severity:"major", reasoning:"..."}], recommendation:"..." }>, expectedRequired:["status","summary","challengedReviewStatus","findingVerdicts","recommendation"], zodRejects:[missing required (delete recommendation), bad enum (status:"go"), bad nested verdict enum (findingVerdicts[0].verdict:"maybe"), bad nested severity enum], stricterThanZod:[extra unknown top-level field, extra unknown nested findingVerdicts field] }. Import skepticResultSchema from ../dist/schemas.js. This proves the generated skeptic JSON Schema is equivalent-or-stricter and deterministic, exactly like worker/review/overseer.

Self-verify: run `npx tsc` until clean, then `npm test` (build + node --test). Report only results actually observed.
risks: executeSkepticRun is a large near-duplicate of executeReviewRun (~300 lines). Mirror via targeted Edits (never rewrite cli.ts); keep the divergences (no applyReviewOutcome, no status/escalation mutation, finding_challenge evidence, skeptic.* events, idle heartbeat on success, no slice-block on parse failure) explicit and commented so a future reader does not 'fix' it back toward the review path.
EvidenceRecord.kind and AgentRole live in src/types.ts which the brief flags as user-owned — keep BOTH additions to single-line union extensions only; do not touch anything else in types.ts.

Independence guard must run before insertAgentRun so a rejected request leaves no agentRun/evidence/event residue (test (c) asserts the ledger is untouched). Placing it after run insertion would create a stale 'running' record.

The fixture review path is deterministic and only ever yields 'accepted' (no source mutation), so the (d) blocked-path regression can only be exercised via a codex fake (like review-runner) — limiting fixture-only coverage to the accepted+verify-passes additivity proof. Acceptable for RE-1; note it rather than over-engineer.

schema-parity's validateAgainstJsonSchema treats optional+absent fields as fine, but ref/dimension being optional means a verdict object with neither is schema-valid; that is intentional (source discriminates) — ensure the 'valid' fixture and zodRejects don't accidentally rely on ref being required.

readLatestReviewGate / verify must keep reading ONLY review_result; since finding_challenge is a new kind its filters already exclude it, but the regression test must explicitly assert verify behavior is identical so a future change can't silently let finding_challenge leak into the gate (that's RE-2).
Default --driver is 'codex'; a developer running `swarm skeptic` without --driver fixture would incur real provider spend. Mitigated in tests (always fixture); the help text notes it.

result.summary: Implemented RE-1 (skeptic foundation, additive only). Surgical types.ts additions ("skeptic" to AgentRole, "finding_challenge" to EvidenceRecord.kind); new skepticFindingVerdictSchema + skepticResultSchema in schemas.ts; skeptic skill binding in protocol.ts reusing reviewer skills; executeSkepticRun in cli.ts mirroring executeReviewRun with an independence guard (rejects reusing the worker/reviewer actor, runs before any run/evidence/event creation, derived from the agent-run ledger), recording kind:"finding_challenge" evidence + skeptic.started/completed/finding_challenged events, and DELIBERATELY never calling applyReviewOutcome or any gate-state mutation; supporting runFixtureSkeptic, buildSkepticPrompt (DEFAULT-REJECT), readSkepticResultFile, printSkepticRunResult, writeSkepticResultSchema (reuses src/schema-json.ts writeSchemaFromZod); new `swarm skeptic` CLI command wired like `swarm review`; SkepticRunResult type. Tests added for both schema-parity (skeptic role) and a new skeptic e2e suite. tsc clean; the accept-gate functions are byte-unchanged.

result.aspect: independence: the skeptic is a distinct role AND actor, never the worker or the reviewer session, with a guard enforcing it
result.evidence:
DISTINCT ROLE (proven by re-reading code): src/types.ts:25 defines `AgentRole = "overseer" | "planner" | "worker" | "verifier" | "reviewer" | "recovery" | "skeptic"` — "skeptic" is a separate member from "worker" and "reviewer". The skeptic agent run is persisted with role:"skeptic" (src/cli.ts:3086, also 3068 for skill binding), whereas the worker uses role:"worker" (src/cli.ts:2472) and the reviewer uses role:"reviewer" (src/cli.ts:2708). So the skeptic is genuinely a distinct role, not a reused worker/reviewer dispatch.

DISTINCT ACTOR + ENFORCING GUARD (proven): src/cli.ts:3019-3031 is the INDEPENDENCE GUARD. It computes priorActors = store.listAgentRuns().filter(run => run.sliceId === slice.id && (run.role === "worker" || run.role === "reviewer")).map(run => run.actor), then `if (priorActors.includes(input.actor)) throw new Error("Skeptic actor must be independent: '...' already acted as worker/reviewer on slice ... Use a distinct --actor.")`. It runs BEFORE any agent run / evidence / event is created (insertAgentRun is later at cli.ts:3083; addEvent at 3105), so a rejected request leaves no residue and the CLI exits non-zero via the thrown error. The guard derives identity from the durable LEDGER, not chat memory: listAgentRuns() reads the SQLite agent_runs table (src/storage.ts:455-506; insertAgentRun persists role+actor at 455-467). The driver dispatch is model-agnostic (validates driver against ["fixture", ...workerDriverIds()] at cli.ts:3015-3017), consistent with worker/reviewer.

TESTS confirm intent: tests/skeptic-runner.e2e.test.js:61-94 (case c) runs worker (guard-worker) + reviewer (guard-reviewer), then asserts that `swarm skeptic` with EITHER reused actor exits non-zero, matches /must be independent|distinct/i, AND leaves the ledger untouched (0 finding_challenge evidence, 0 skeptic agent runs). Case (a) (lines 16-38) asserts the skeptic actor differs from both worker and reviewer actors and is recorded as role:"skeptic". Defaults also do not collide: worker default actor "worker" (cli.ts:889), reviewer "reviewer" (cli.ts:946), skeptic "skeptic" (cli.ts:972).
result.gaps:
1. "Reviewer SESSION" is enforced at ACTOR granularity, not at provider-session granularity. AgentRunRecord has a separate sessionId field (src/types.ts:162; persisted in storage.ts:458-466), but the guard keys solely on `actor` (cli.ts:3026-3027), never on sessionId. This matches how worker/reviewer identity is modeled everywhere (actor is the durable identity), so it is a defensible reading of "session/actor" — but a same-reviewer provider session re-invoked under a deliberately different --actor string would NOT be caught. Independence is only as strong as the operator's choice of distinct actor ids.
2. The guard scopes priorActors to run.sliceId === slice.id, so the same actor that reviewed/worked a DIFFERENT slice could skeptic THIS slice. That is the correct per-slice semantics for RE-1 (independence is per work item), not a defect, but worth noting the guard is slice-scoped.
3. The guard intentionally does not block reusing a prior SKEPTIC actor (filter is worker/reviewer only), so the same skeptic actor can re-run; acceptable since a skeptic is not the party whose work is being judged.
None of these undermine the core claim: the skeptic is a distinct role with a real, ledger-backed, pre-side-effect guard that rejects reuse of the worker or reviewer actor for the slice.
